security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG implements Smip fast interrupt entry/exit with the old conditional stack-swap behavior (cspspush during save, cspspop during restore), but guest software is written against the new spec where context is saved directly on the interrupted context's own stack — no swap occurs — causing the handler to save/restore to the wrong memory region
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: cspspush OR cspspop in interrupt-entry/exit TCG translation; conditional stack-swap logic in CLIC/Smip trap handling path; stack pointer swap gating on xsp/SPP state during hwint save-restore
affected_entities: Smip/CLIC hardware interrupt save-restore sequence (ipush/ipop or equivalent micro-architectural state machine)
security_spec.summary: Stale conditional stack-swap (cspspush/cspspop) in QEMU interrupt entry/exit corrupts interrupted-context stack when guest targets post-PR#691 no-swap behavior

findings.finding: Smip fast interrupt entry/exit (cspspush, cspspop, CLIC, MNXTI, stack-swap) is completely absent from this QEMU codebase. No conditional stack-swap logic exists in TCG translation, interrupt handling, or CSR emulation paths. The vulnerability described in the security spec cannot trigger because the feature is unimplemented.
findings.snippet: N/A — Smip is not implemented in this QEMU version

findings.finding: The generic RISC-V interrupt entry path has no Smip-specific logic. Only RNMI gating exists (line 2242), which is a separate extension. No cspspush/cspspop or stack-swap occurs during interrupt delivery.
MRET handler contains RNMI restore logic (mnstatus.NMIE, MNPELP, MNPP), but no Smip cspspop or stack-swap restore. The RNMI exit path is correctly scoped to the RNMI extension.
